claims.text: The base alloy is equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
As-cast HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
As-cast HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Undoped HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance that causes mechanical-performance losses at high temperature.
Approximately 2–5 at% Al can be incorporated into HfNbTaTiZr by vacuum arc or induction melting followed by casting.
A 2–5 at% Al addition will produce a continuous, stable Al2O3 surface scale during exposure at 1000 °C in air.
The proposed alumina scale will act as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
Blocking oxygen diffusion will mitigate detrimental oxygen ingress into the alloy.
Al-doped HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit significantly lower oxidation mass gain than undoped HfNbTaTiZr after exposure at 1000 °C in air for up to 100 h.
The Al-modified alloy will retain at least approximately 80–90% of the base alloy's yield strength.
The Al-modified alloy will retain at least approximately 80–90% of the base alloy's ductility.
The proposed benefit is applicable at approximately 1000 °C in air for extended exposure and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Higher Al concentrations or more extreme conditions may alter phase stability and microstructure.
The optimal Al content and processing conditions remain to be established experimentally.

contradictions.description: The conditions specify exposure for up to 100 h, whereas the boundary describes applicability for durations of at least 100 h, leaving the claimed duration range internally inconsistent beyond the single 100 h point.

The conditions describe high-temperature exposure under mechanical loading, but the experiment exposes specimens first and performs tensile loading afterward; it therefore does not test concurrent oxidation and loading as stated.
